blocks.text: Harbor & Oak Shopify theme v1 requirements

This is the working cut for HBR-1104 on June 18, 2020. Dana Whitlock asked for a written bound after the current path (Stock Debut, 412 SKUs, 1.8s LCP on product from Jenna's April capture) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Dana Whitlock, Jenna Park, and Nia Brooks. Primary host shop.harbor.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on Brightlane Theme Co overlay, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

Fork Debut. Four templates: home, collection, product, cart. Reject Brightlane Theme Co ($6.8k, no local-pickup slot). I am not restating a hallway yes. Brightlane Theme Co overlay is out because Quote had a single-tenant slider pack and no local-pickup template. Dana needs pickup more than a slider. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at skus=412, lcp=1.8, target=2.4, cost=6.8, templates=4, photos=2.1, weeks=7, conv=1.14. Sibling tickets HBR-REQ-2020-008 and HBR-TDD-2020-021. I will not reopen Brightlane Theme Co overlay in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Jenna Park is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

blocks.text: Fork Debut. Four templates: home, collection, product, cart. Reject Brightlane Theme Co ($6.8k, no local-pickup slot).

Ticket HBR-1104 names the pull. If those numbers moved after June 18, 2020, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in Slack.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Nia Brooks owns a leftover that is easy to skip: stg-shop.harbor.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (09): refuse on Brightlane Theme Co overlay, lock is four templates, LCP under 2.4s on product, pickup stub in cart. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on HBR-REQ-2020-008.
I need the jacket photos to load before the add-to-cart button. I do not need another homepage slider.

What a skeptical user would try first on shop.harbor.internal: the path Dana Whitlock actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on theme-preview.harbor.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

theme-preview.harbor.internal is in this file because skipping it is how the last near-miss happened. Nia Brooks owns the check. I want a count on HBR-TDD-2020-021 before anyone says the leftover is 'implied.' Implied leftovers are how Brightlane Theme Co overlay almost returned.
What I will not claim in HBR-REQ-2020-008

I will not claim Brightlane Theme Co overlay is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host shop.harbor.internal.
First useful slice for HBR-1104

First useful is four templates, LCP under 2.4s on product, pickup stub in cart, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Dana Whitlock sees that slice on shop.harbor.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Dana Whitlock is in the thread. I will not hide it inside HBR-REQ-2020-008.
Support zip and identifiers (09)

A support zip for this work goes through redaction. Customer email, card PAN, and passwords come back. Pressure is not a reason to paste them into HBR-1104. Michael Gilfilian will bounce the zip. Host if we have to prove a redaction: stg-shop.harbor.internal.
